# Norman Douglas

## Overview

- **Age:** Over fifty  <sub>[v5 c15 P28](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0028)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c2 P46](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0046)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v5 c35 P0](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** Glen St. Mary / Four Winds region  <sub>[v5 c15 P27](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0027), [v5 c21 P0](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v5 c16 P23](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0023), [v5 c16 P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Old pagan  <sub>[v5 c16 P37](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0037)</sub>; Old reprobate  <sub>[v5 c16 P78](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0078)</sub>

## Appearance

Norman Douglas is a tall, broad-shouldered, and fine-looking man with a Roman nose, frank blue eyes, a high white forehead, and an athletic, powerful frame. For fifteen years he maintained an unkempt appearance with a great river of crinkly brown-red beard reaching nearly to his knees and a corresponding cascade of thick, wavy brown-red hair down his back. After shaving his beard and cutting his hair, he retained his high-colored, red-haired, and red-bearded look, keeping his bold, striking features.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P13](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0013), [v4 c35 P33](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0033), [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028), [v5 c16 P53](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0053), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001)_

## Personality

Norman Douglas is a boisterous, stubborn, and outspoken man who possesses an explosive temper and a booming voice. He delights in shouting, roaring with laughter, and engaging in spirited, uncompromising arguments, particularly regarding politics or religion. Despite his fierce demeanor, he respects spirit and 'spunk' in others, holds no grudges after his quick outbursts, and harbors a genuinely kind, generous heart beneath his rough exterior. He is famously independent, undaunted by public opinion, and enjoys a good laugh, even at his own expense.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P33](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0033), [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059), [v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c16 P54](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0054), [v5 c16 P59](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0059), [v5 c16 P79](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0079), [v5 c16 P80](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0080)_

## History

During a fiercely contested general election fifteen years prior, Norman Douglas made a vow at a public meeting that he would neither shave his face nor cut his hair until the Liberal party (Grits) returned to power. As the Conservatives remained in office, he maintained his vow for a decade and a half, growing a long, flowing beard and mane of hair that made him famous across Four Winds. When the Liberals finally won a general election years later, he immediately went to the local barber in the middle of the night, forced him to shave his beard and trim his hair, and abandoned his wild appearance. Soon afterward, he began attending church again, renewing his acquaintance with his old flame, Ellen West, whom he had courted thirty years earlier before marrying his late wife Hester. Despite an initial impasse caused by a vow Ellen and her sister Rosemary had made, Faith Meredith intervened to resolve their misunderstandings, leading Norman to propose directly. Ellen accepted his proposal, and the two were married in a double wedding alongside Reverend John Meredith and Rosemary West, after which Norman moved to Ellen's farm on the hill.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P33](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0033), [v4 c35 P28](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0028), [v4 c35 P30](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0030), [v5 c15 P28](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0028), [v5 c15 P30](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0030), [v5 c21 P12](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0012), [v5 c22 P1](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0001), [v5 c34 P38](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0038), [v5 c35 P0](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Born into a notoriously stubborn family of political Grits in the Four Winds region  <sub>[v4 c9 P33](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0033), [v4 c9 P35](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0035)</sub>
- Courted Ellen West in his youth before a bitter quarrel parted them  <sub>[v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c15 P30](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0030)</sub>
- Married Hester Reese on a rebound, whom he survived  <sub>[v5 c15 P30](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0030), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031)</sub>
- Left the Presbyterian church for twenty years after a dispute over a cow deal with a session member  <sub>[v5 c15 P28](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0028)</sub>
